name: brightwood_tracker_takes_one_creature_from_top_four_rest_to_bottom
notes: Printed: '{5}{G}, {T}: Look at the top four cards of your library. You may reveal a creature card from among them and put it into your hand. Put the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order.' Top four (top first): Instant A, Creature B, Land C, Creature D; Creature D goes to hand, the other three go to the bottom (order unasserted), the unseen fifth card (Creature E) is on top after. Decision words are literal (card:2 = Creature D by pack order): on an activate step a pack key would fall through the executor's decision pool to the runner's provider queue, which restarts at the first word. This was its G4 spec pack tools/scenarios/cards/M20/brightwood_tracker_1.json. Parked here when the record's REST move gained arrange RANDOM ('in a random order'; without it the engine now asks the owner the order, CR 401.4): the tree changed, so the record is not applied until a verifier re-verifies it, and games play the compiler's tree, which has no activated ability. It passes against the record's tree (cardtool runpack), asking no order; re-verifying the card brings it back.
